'''Phillip Augustus Griffiths IV''' (born October 18, 1938) is an American mathematician, known for his work in the field of [[geometry]], and in particular for the [[complex manifold]] approach to [[algebraic geometry]]. He is a major developer in particular of the theory of [[variation of Hodge structure]] in [[Hodge theory]] and [[moduli theory]], which forms part of transcendental algebraic geometry and which also touches upon major and distant areas of [[differential geometry]]. He also worked on partial differential equations, coauthored with [[Shiing-Shen Chern]], [[Robert Bryant (mathematician)|Robert Bryant]] and [[Robert Brown Gardner|Robert Gardner]] on exterior differential systems.

==Education==
Griffiths received his BS from [[Wake Forest College]] in 1959.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Poovey (P '08) |first=Cherin C. |date=2014-02-04 |title=Prize of a lifetime |url=https://magazine.wfu.edu/2014/02/04/prize-of-a-lifetime/ |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=Wake Forest Magazine |language=en}}</ref> He received his PhD from [[Princeton University]] in 1962 after completing a doctoral dissertation, titled "On certain homogeneous [[complex manifold]]s", under the supervision of [[Donald C. Spencer|Donald Spencer]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Griffith|first=Phillip|url=https://catalog.princeton.edu/catalog/2080987|title=On certain homogeneous complex manifolds|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|date=1962|volume=48|issue=5|pages=780–3|doi=10.1073/pnas.48.5.780|pmid=16590943|pmc=220851|bibcode=1962PNAS...48..780G|language=en|doi-access=free}}</ref> 

== Career ==
Afterwards, he held positions at [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1962–1967) and Princeton University (1967–1972).{{citation needed|date=September 2020}} Griffiths was a professor of mathematics at [[Harvard University]] from 1972 to 1983.<ref name="IAS" /> He was then a Provost and James B. Duke Professor of Mathematics at [[Duke University]] from 1983 to 1991.<ref name="IAS" /> From 1991 to 2003, he was the Director of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (IAS) in [[Princeton, New Jersey]].<ref name="IAS" /> He remained as part of the Faculty of Mathematics at the IAS until June 2009, after which he has been emeritus at the IAS.<ref name="IAS" /> He has published on algebraic geometry, [[differential geometry]], [[geometric function theory]], and the geometry of [[partial differential equations]].

Griffiths serves as the Chair of the [[Science Initiative Group]].<ref name="IAS">{{cite web |url=http://www.ias.edu/people/faculty-and-emeriti/griffiths |publisher=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |title=Phillip A. Griffiths |date=December 9, 2019 |access-date=September 11, 2020}}</ref> He is co-author, with [[Joe Harris (mathematician)|Joe Harris]], of ''Principles of Algebraic Geometry'', a well-regarded textbook on [[complex number|complex]] [[algebraic geometry]].<ref>[http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?service=UI&version=1.0&verb=Display&handle=euclid.bams/1183545213 Review: Phillip Griffiths and Joseph Harris, Principles of algebraic geometry] by [[Joseph Lipman]]</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Griffiths was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1979 and the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 1992.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Phillip A. Griffiths |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/phillip-a-griffiths-eqlmjb/ |access-date=March 28, 2022 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Member History |url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Phillip+Griffiths&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced |access-date=March 28, 2022 |website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref> In 2008, he was awarded the [[Wolf Prize]] (jointly with [[Deligne]] and [[David Mumford|Mumford]])<ref>{{cite web | title=The Wolf Foundation Prize in Mathematics | url=http://www.wolffund.org.il/index.php?dir=site&page=winners&name=&prize=3016&year=&field=3004}}</ref> and the [[Brouwer Medal]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/news/press-releases/2009-14 |title=Institute for Advanced Study: Royal Dutch Mathematical Society Awards Tri-annual Brouwer Prize to Phillip A. Griffiths |access-date=February 9, 2016 |archive-date=February 16, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160216045902/https://www.ias.edu/news/press-releases/2009-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved January 19, 2013.</ref> Moreover, in 2014 Griffiths was awarded the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Lifetime Achievement by the American Mathematical Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS :: Leroy P. Steele Prize (1970 - 1992) |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/prizes-awards/paview-inactive.cgi?parent_id=28 |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=www.ams.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Poovey (P '08) |first=Cherin C. |date=2014-02-04 |title=Prize of a lifetime |url=https://magazine.wfu.edu/2014/02/04/prize-of-a-lifetime/ |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=Wake Forest Magazine |language=en}}</ref> Also in 2014, Griffiths was awarded the [[Chern Medal]] for lifetime devotion to mathematics and outstanding achievements by the [[International Mathematical Union]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BREAKING NEWS: IAS Professor Emeritus Awarded Chern Medal – Town Topics |url=https://www.towntopics.com/2014/08/15/breaking-news-ias-professor-emeritus-awarded-chern-medal/ |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=www.towntopics.com}}</ref>
